page.layout: One printed page: running head and page number at top; one text column at right with two lines of Arabic and Hebrew mixed into Latin; narrow notes in the left margin beside the text; digitiser credit at bottom right (not transcribed).

main_text.p: AlGazali.[?الاعراب يتيما ضعيفا مهتضعفا] concesserit illi Deus hæc omnia cum ipse Idiota esset, qui nulli unquam scientiæ operam dederit, nec libros pervolverit, nec scientiam acquirendæ gratiâ peregrinatus fuerit, sed semper manserit inter Arabum ignorantissimos, orphanus & impotens, ac pro impotenti habitus. Alia ab ipso patrâta miracula mille, vel (juxtà alios) ter mille numerari, refert Al Jannabius, at in uno Alcorano 60. ferè millia (quot forsan versiculos) contineri. Quanti autem apud eos ponderis, hoc in genere, habeatur Alcoranus, meminit etiam Judas Levita in lib: Cozari, ubi Ismaelita Regi Cozarorum religionis suæ rationem reddens, inter cætera hæc affert [?ונורחה כי ספר תורתנו דברי אלהים והוא] [?בעצמו מופת התחייבנו בקבולו בעבור עצמן מפני שאין ארם יכול לחבר ספר אחר כמוהו ולא כפרשה אחת] [?מפרשותיו] l. 1. Profitemur autem librum Legis nostræ esse verba Dei, atque esse cum in se miraculum quod {*}suis ip-sius gratiâ recipere tenemur, quòd non fit homo qui alium ipsi similem librum componere possit; nec vel capitulum unum ex ipsius capitulis. Hanc enim genuinam esse lectionem, ut ita respondeat Arabum [?سكنورتمش سوره], extra controversiam est, cùm alias legatur [?נפרש] & responendum putet Juda Moskati [?נפרש]. Non gravabitur autem forsan Lector oculos conjicere in ea quæ ad exemplarium quibus usus sum alterius marginem adscripta reperi; Cùm quidam Gregorium nostrum, quod de Miraculorum Mohammedi adscriptorum fide detrahere videatur, ut blasphemiæ reum convitiis & diris prosecutus esset, opposuit Scalius quidam qui ea legerat, hæc verba, [?مصنف هذا الكتاب وان كان ضرايا لكنه في هذا المجل غير]* Potiùs quàm ut Juda Moskati, propter excellentiam suam.

page.notes: The first Arabic line (top of column) and the Arabic at the foot of the column are partly illegible; they are given as best read and marked [?]. The Hebrew lines after "affert" are read with doubt, especially the line ending "מפרשותיו". The Arabic in "سكنورتمش سوره" and the Hebrew "נפרש" (twice) are doubtful. The last Arabic line is only partly legible. The Latin "Alcorano" and "Al Jannabius" may be set in italic or roman; read as italic. The reference mark "*" in the text is set beside "quod" and matches the note. No catchword or signature is printed. The digitiser credit at the bottom right is excluded.
